page: Microsoft Azure E4-2as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EASv4 server family. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 1 physical core supporting 2 threads (2 vCPUs), 32.0 GB of system memory, and 66 GB of local storage. The CPU features a 32 MB L3 cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache, with support for AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_ni, BMI2, ADX, and FMA instructions. It runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25% at 2690.99. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core performance of 2697.38 and Geekbench multi-core score of 1975.0 fall into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively, reflecting the dual-thread single-core physical layout. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block bandwidth at 32.63 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 22.38 GB/sec. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E4-2as_v4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per core, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing power. Given the lower performance in database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded compiling, this instance is best suited for lightweight memory-bound tasks, single-threaded applications, basic caching, or development environments requiring a larger memory footprint without high CPU core density.
